frontier.hypothesis: The `expand_binop` commutative swap on the shipped form can be defeated by changing the EXPANSION TARGET rather than the syntax — a construct that makes GCC expand the *3 sum into an anonymous temp (`target == 0`, so no swap test fires) which is later coalesced into `idx`'s register.
frontier.mechanism: optabs.c:399-417 swaps a commutative operand pair whenever the expansion target IS op1, so `idx = <x> + idx;` always expands as (plus idx x) — visible in the .rtl dump before cse runs. Eight source-level respellings are measured dead (s3 H11) and random search over ~40k iterations on this chassis found nothing (s5 H21), so the remaining surface is which C constructs cause expand_expr to call expand_binop with target == 0 at all.
frontier.next_probe: Read expr.c's expand_assignment / expand_expr store path (the TREE_CODE (to) == VAR_DECL case and the paths that force a temp: assignment used as a value, compound assignment through a cast, a differently-typed or narrower view of the destination), enumerate the constructs that yield target == 0, and sandbox each on the shipped body. Confirm from the .rtl dump (tmp/grind/func_800645B0/s2/dumpvar.sh + dumpAA.py) that the emitted insn is (plus idx2 idx) before trusting the score.

frontier.hypothesis: In the DA shape (byte offset routed through `idx`, sum in `wid`) local_alloc can be made to give $s0 to the multi-block `idx` instead of to the block-local `idx2`, which would close all three constraints at once.
frontier.mechanism: local_alloc runs before global_alloc. In the shipped/CA shape the pseudo that claims $s0 from local_alloc is the byte-offset CSE temp — block-local, but live across all four rand() calls, so it needs a callee-save — and `idx2` is pushed to $s1. In DA that claimant is gone, so `idx2` takes $s0 and `idx` is left $s1 by global_alloc; the whole 12-point cost of DA is that swap, and the target's own allocation proves the wanted state is reachable.
frontier.next_probe: Read local-alloc.c's block_alloc / find_free_reg ordering (qty priority, qty_phys_reg suggestions, accept_call_clobbered), dump .lreg/.greg for DA and for the shipped form side by side, then look for a C shape in which the halfword-offset value is NOT a block-local pseudo (genuinely referenced in the loop-top block) or in which some other block-local callee-save-needing value out-prioritises it, and sandbox each.

frontier.hypothesis: The original's inner-loop pseudo set differs from all three near-miss shapes, and the difference is visible by comparing their .sched/.greg state against what the target's 78 instructions imply.
frontier.mechanism: SB (shipped), CA and IA are each exactly one instruction away and each fails on a DIFFERENT fully-named GCC decision (expand_binop swap / birthing_insn_p bonus / entry-copy constant fold). That is the signature of a shape that is close to but not the original. Permuter has now also been ruled out as a way to stumble onto the original from either chassis, which raises the value of the forensic comparison.
frontier.next_probe: Dump t.i.sched and t.i.greg for SB, CA and IA with tmp/grind/func_800645B0/s2/dumpvar.sh + dumpAA.py, extract the inner-loop block's insn list and register dispositions for each, and diff them against the target's instruction sequence to identify a pseudo count or live-range shape none of the three produces.
